name: bird-02-closed-loop-liveness
question:
When BiRDTransportProcess is coupled to the Phase-1 MonodCellProcess at a
static high biomass density, does the reactor→cell feedback fire —
dissolved O2 dropping below saturation as consumption outpaces transport —
with O2 mass balance closing across cell and reactor contributions?
hypothesis:
At an impactful biomass density, steady-state dissolved O2 settles below
saturation, d[O2]/dt equals reactor transport minus cell consumption at
every step, and removing the biomass input returns O2 to saturation —
confirming a live, bidirectional loop.
objective:
Compose BiRDTransportProcess with MonodCellProcess at a constant high
biomass density and measure dissolved O2 and the O2 balance to determine
that the closed loop is live, not merely wired.
description:
This is the integration test the single-process reactor cannot provide:
the reactor→cell direction only fires when biomass is dense enough to
perturb reactor state. The Phase-1 MonodCellProcess supplies biomass and
an O2 consumption flux under the cell-side contract; a constant scale
factor on a representative biomass is sufficient here — no growth dynamics
are needed to establish liveness.

Distinct from bird-01's per-edge unit checks, this study exercises the
composed loop end-to-end and asserts mass-balance closure across the two
processes' contributions at the shared dissolved-O2 store.

expected_behavior.name: dissolved-o2-drops-below-saturation-at-high-biomass
expected_behavior.en: At a high biomass density, steady-state dissolved O2 settles below the saturation concentration — consumption outpacing transport pulls DO down, showing the reactor→cell direction fires.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird02_liveness.py::test_do_drops_below_saturation_at_high_biomass — at 5 g/L (growth off), steady-state DO settles below C*_O2 and stays non-negative.

expected_behavior.name: o2-mass-balance-closes
expected_behavior.en: d[O2]/dt equals reactor transport minus cell consumption at every step within tolerance — the two processes' deltas aggregate at the shared store without double-counting or leakage.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird02_liveness.py::test_o2_mass_balance_closes_process_math (d[O2] == transport − consumption, computed independently) and ::test_o2_mass_balance_closes_in_composite (the shared store aggregates both deltas). The cell emits o2_exchange_delta so the balance is observable.

expected_behavior.name: dissolved-o2-recovers-when-biomass-removed
expected_behavior.en: Setting the biomass input to zero returns dissolved O2 to saturation, confirming the feedback is bidirectional and not a fixed offset.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird02_liveness.py::test_do_recovers_when_biomass_removed — with negligible biomass, transport restores depleted DO to ~C*_O2 (8.21 mg/L).

report.conclusion: Green. Baseline ran (runs[] recorded) and every acceptance behavior is verified by a passing pytest verifier (tests/test_bird02_liveness.py). Coupling the transport process to the Monod cell at high biomass fires the reactor->cell feedback - dissolved O2 drops below air saturation as consumption outpaces transport - and recovers toward saturation when biomass is removed; the O2 mass balance closes.

regression_compatibility.basis: Workspace builds and the full suite is green (51 passed); the baseline composite runs cleanly through the workbench.

biological_validation.basis: Behavior verifiers pass (tests/test_bird02_liveness.py): DO drops below saturation at high biomass, O2 mass balance residual ~0, and DO recovers to the saturation band when biomass is removed.

explanatory_gain.basis: Demonstrates a live closed loop: the reactor and cell engine exchange dissolved O2 additively at the shared store, so net dO2/dt = transport - consumption is exercised at impactful density.
